title: Moment constants split into density-calibrated geometry and prime arithmetic
claim: The random-matrix contribution to a zeta-moment constant is a universal geometric factor only after matrix size is matched to local zero density; the missing source-specific information is a prime Euler factor. In the Dirichlet-series representation, this split is concrete: pairwise zeta poles carry the universal singular growth, while a regular Euler product carries the arithmetic constant.
historical_or_program_relation: The characteristic-polynomial prediction highlighted in the 2003 overview is refined by arithmetic derivations and hybrid models that identify exactly what the unitary ensemble forgets, and the 2025 survey retains density matching and restoration of prime data as separate steps.
limits: The higher zeta-moment asymptotics remain conjectural; density matching does not derive an operator or a universality theorem, and neither the matrix model nor the pole extraction alone proves the arithmetic-to-geometric factorization for zeta.

title: Gaussian bulk predicts the moment exponent but not constants or extreme regimes
claim: A Gaussian model for log absolute zeta values produces the conjectural quadratic moment exponent through its moment-generating function, but this bulk limit neither fixes the arithmetic-normalized constants nor controls the entire tail. Pole-dominated small-value behavior and the change from quadratic to V log V large-deviation decay require representations beyond the local cumulant expansion.
historical_or_program_relation: Keating and Snaith separated Selberg-type Gaussianity from moment asymptotics and identified a pole-controlled regime; later tail theorems and the modern moment survey make the resulting regime split an explicit constraint on probabilistic moment heuristics.
limits: The cited tail bounds and moment heuristics have different hypotheses and parameter ranges. Agreement on the logarithmic exponent is not agreement on constants, and no single cited unit establishes a complete zeta value distribution.

title: Prime-frequency pairing is the arithmetic surrogate for Gaussian moments
claim: Time averaging of short prime polynomials kills every cosine monomial unless prime multiplicities pair, so square support and multiplicativity factor the surviving terms prime by prime. Truncated exponentials or Bessel generating products then package those diagonal pairings into the same variance exponential that a Gaussian cumulant calculation produces.
historical_or_program_relation: The random-matrix cumulant route and later deterministic prime-polynomial proofs meet at a common combinatorial mechanism: bounded higher cumulants on one side correspond to admissible diagonal pairings on the other.
limits: Oscillatory orthogonality is not literal probabilistic independence and is valid only within polynomial-length and moment-order budgets. Gaussianizing small primes can erase the arithmetic factor, and the mechanism does not by itself control off-diagonal or extreme contributions.

title: Moments and tails convert in both directions only with scale-adapted budgets
claim: Layer-cake integration turns large-deviation level sets into shifted-moment bounds, while Markov's inequality applied to high even prime-polynomial moments turns mean values back into tail bounds. Sharp use of either direction requires choosing the moment order and prime-block truncation according to variance, deviation size, and the admissible polynomial or interval length.
historical_or_program_relation: The shifted-moment method organized correlations into a variance parameter and optimized moment order across Gaussian and exponential tails; later short-interval and multiscale moment arguments make the capacity constraint and rare-event disposal explicit.
limits: These are inequality bridges, not an equivalence of distributions. Their conditional assumptions, smoothing, shift geometry, and interval constraints differ, and an optimizer outside the admissible length range gives only a heuristic scale.

title: Long polynomials reveal a length-graded filtration of off-diagonal moment terms
claim: Increasing Dirichlet-polynomial length does more than improve approximation: it activates new off-diagonal correlation strata. In the moment recipe these strata are graded by swap cardinality; in the divisor-correlation calculation they appear as rational-direction discrepancy strata, and collecting all allowed strata reproduces the swaps selected by the length.
historical_or_program_relation: The impossible negative values of conventional long-polynomial heuristics provide a sign-based failure detector; the later swap and Type-II programs propose the missing structural correction and match its grades through arithmetic stratification.
limits: Nonnegativity falsifies an incomplete heuristic but does not identify a unique repair or disprove the moment conjecture. The swap recipe and the all-strata correspondence remain part of a conjectural higher-moment program rather than a proof of the full zeta moments.

title: The off-diagonal pair-correlation barrier is a shifted-prime correlation problem
claim: Once the Dirichlet polynomial is too long for diagonal Parseval control, zero pair correlation is governed by off-diagonal sums of Lambda(n)Lambda(n+h). Reindexing prime powers with the von Mangoldt function isolates this shifted statistic, while a transition-range evaluation imports Twin Prime singular-series information for the off diagonal and treats diagonal prime squares separately under RH.
historical_or_program_relation: Montgomery identified shifted prime powers as the obstruction beyond the first Fourier band; the quantum-chaos derivation reached the same arithmetic intermediate object, and later transition formulas made the distinct diagonal and Twin-Prime-dependent burdens explicit.
limits: The reductions use smoothing, averaging, and restricted shift or scale regimes. Twin Prime input is conditional, replacing a fluctuating shifted product by its mean is unresolved in the cited lecture, and proof-search failure here would not refute pair correlation.

title: Fourier support is an arithmetic complexity budget for zero statistics
claim: Band-limited test functions make zero-difference statistics observable from known frequency data and can force approximate multiplicative balance of prime-power products to become exact integer equality, thereby suppressing the off diagonal. Widening the support asks for richer spacing information but simultaneously lengthens the arithmetic polynomial until diagonal control no longer closes.
historical_or_program_relation: Montgomery's support-limited convolution interface is recast in later pair-correlation extremal problems as an admissibility contract and in n-level calculations as the precise localization that converts analytic near-balance into arithmetic equality.
limits: Support-restricted statistics do not determine the full zero process or unrestricted gap distribution. The cited pair- and n-level results use different hypotheses and normalizations, and the diagonalization mechanism fails rather than automatically extending when the support budget is exceeded.

title: Symmetry survives in centers and moment constants, but averaging weights can mimic it
claim: After a common Gaussian variance scale hides ensemble distinctions, symmetry reappears in lower-order data: prime-square survival shifts the mean of log central values, while Gamma and Barnes-G moment functions encode ensemble-specific constants. Low-zero family statistics add separate rank and root-number channels, and changing from counting measure to a trace-formula weight can alter the observed density without changing the underlying representation type.
historical_or_program_relation: Random-matrix symmetry fingerprints progressed from ensemble moment formulas to arithmetic explanations of family-dependent centering; the automorphic-family program then exposed measure choice and central atoms as independent confounds in reading symmetry from statistics.
limits: The units concern different families and observables, and several distributional statements are predictions or GRH-compatible bounds rather than full limit theorems. A weighted density cannot be identified with the unweighted symmetry type until the weights are removed or controlled.

title: Inverse-density shifts decide whether moments separate or coalesce
claim: The invariant separation is the raw shift multiplied by local zero density. At that microscopic scale, two shifted observables retain partial correlation and coalescing shifts behave like one higher moment; when the observation is conditioned at a zero, a spherical-Bessel crossover interpolates from derivative moments at zero displacement toward ordinary field moments as the scaled displacement grows.
historical_or_program_relation: Shifted characteristic-polynomial moments first organized merging singularities by inverse mean spacing; the zero-conditioned crossover program extends the same scale principle to connect discrete derivative moments and continuous value moments.
limits: The two crossovers have different conditioning and are not a single proved zeta theorem. The zeta transfer is conjectural, interchange of limits needs uniformity, and the recorded far-offset passage has a domain gap for scaled parameters beyond the displayed range.

title: Mollified mean squares turn zero counts into constrained variational objectives
claim: Littlewood or Jensen reductions replace zero geometry by the mean square of a differential combination times a Mobius mollifier. Once an analytic mean-value theorem exposes dependence on coefficient profiles, zero-density progress becomes constrained optimization: a quadratic Euler-Lagrange problem for one profile, a six-component scalar objective for multi-piece mollifiers, or a polynomial approximation to a limiting sinh profile for high derivative order.
historical_or_program_relation: Conrey's variational closure of Levinson's method becomes a reusable interface: later work enlarges the mollifier into interacting pieces and reuses the same mean-square constant to optimize derivative-zero densities.
limits: The optimization is licensed only by the stated mollifier-length and uniform-shift estimates. Continuous optimizers or displayed numerical witnesses need admissible polynomial approximation and do not certify a global optimum; the conclusions are aggregate zero proportions, not pointwise zero locations.

title: Moment asymptotics are encoded by universal poles plus regular arithmetic residues
claim: Multiplicative diagonal constraints factor a moment-generating Dirichlet series into standard pairwise zeta poles and a holomorphic Euler product carrying local arithmetic. Matching the same singular parts in different coordinates yields residue identities, while for quadratic families a further averaging variable moves the mean-value problem to the residue of a corrected multiple Dirichlet series at w=1.
historical_or_program_relation: Height-aspect moment calculations and shifted-divisor identities established residue data as the stable interface; the multiple-Dirichlet-series program extends that interface so family averaging and functional-equation symmetries can be studied in one several-variable object.
limits: The height and family problems are not interchangeable. Extracting the diagonal residue does not supply reflected polar terms, analytic continuation, Tauberian hypotheses, or the final moment theorem, and the central quadratic-family specialization remains an explicit proof burden.

title: Shared prime ancestry links mesoscopic covariance to multiscale extreme-value proofs
claim: Nearby log-zeta values have a capped minimum covariance that can be realized by shared Gaussian increments along an ancestor tree. Extreme-value arguments use the same geometry operationally: prime blocks are variance-matched, a shared low-frequency trunk is removed when changing window scale, and second-moment or entropy-amplitude optimization counts paths that remain high across blocks rather than isolated terminal spikes.
historical_or_program_relation: The mesoscopic central-limit description makes the genealogy an exact covariance representation; later local-maximum and free-energy proofs turn that representation into a proof architecture based on correlated trials and multiscale high-point paths.
limits: A finite-dimensional Gaussian limit is not a pathwise field and does not imply an extreme-value law. The tree representation proves covariance positivity, not zeta maxima; the cited maximum and free-energy results use additional mollification, comparison, moment, and scale-specific estimates.

title: Derivative moments form an operational interface from microscopic zeros to large gaps
claim: Microscopic displacement from a zero organizes a crossover whose zero-offset limit is a derivative moment, while random-matrix formulas make the corresponding derivative constants explicit. Wirtinger inequalities then consume value and derivative moments as global integral data and convert them into lower bounds for exceptional normalized gaps between critical-line zeros.
historical_or_program_relation: The characteristic-polynomial program does more than predict standalone constants: the discrete-to-continuous crossover identifies the derivative endpoint, and the gap program supplies a downstream analytic consumer for those constants.
limits: The derivative-moment asymptotics and much of the zeta crossover are conjectural, with a recorded uniformity gap at part of the far-offset passage. Random-matrix constants make the inequality numerically evaluable but do not prove the zeta input or RH, and moment inequalities force some large gaps without determining the full spacing law.

title: Finite matrix size is a density calibration, not disposable error
claim: Matching matrix dimension to the local mean density makes finite-N characteristic-polynomial laws the relevant comparison at finite zeta height. Structured non-Gaussian deviations and slow convergence of low-zero or local-maximum data are therefore compatible with asymptotic unitary universality rather than immediate counterexamples to it.
historical_or_program_relation: Montgomery's original unitary analogy already warned that low-zero numerics could converge slowly; finite-N moment and density calculations later promoted that warning into a calibrated model, while extreme-value experiments exposed the remaining arithmetic finite-height corrections.
limits: Finite-N agreement is supportive modeling evidence, not a proof of zeta universality. Random matrices omit prime arithmetic, the cited numerical observables are not identical, and slow convergence cannot be invoked to explain away arbitrary discrepancies.
